terms.comment: Literally “to dig out”. Traupman has quicquam ēruere dē (+ abl.); but quicquam belongs in negative sentences and questions, so in a plain statement aliquid ēruere dē ….

phrases.latin: mī sīcundē potes, ēruēs, quī decem lēgātī Mummiō fuerint
phrases.english: dig up for me, if you can from anywhere, who the ten commissioners with Mummius were

sources: Lewis & Short: eruo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 96, 304.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
